structured.approach: Attempt 2. The refusal said the cited repository files had not been read in this session, so I re-read every one of them here: ap_forecast/.git/HEAD, .git/config, .git/logs/refs/heads/feature/story, .git/logs/refs/heads/dev, ci.py, CLAUDE.md, src/ap_forecast/__init__.py, predict.py and explain.py. I also re-read org.engineering_stack and searched feat.tasks again for the lane's tasks. The hook allows no shell commands in this step, so the repository state comes from these files and the tool view. I rewrote task.repo_access in full, and every file it cites was read in this session. Two things changed from attempt 1. I removed the rows that rested on a directory listing instead of a read, such as the claim that tests/test_forecast.py exists. I also dropped a stray '[Tool result]' line that someone else had appended to the earlier draft. I didn't use any connector.

claims.text: The Data Science lane's tasks TSK-03 (STORY-03) and TSK-04 (STORY-04) both target ap_forecast; no new repository is needed.
Repository ap_forecast is available locally, the working tree is clean and the agent identity has write access.
HEAD points to refs/heads/feature/story, which was created at commit d67e866; dev was created from origin/dev at d67e866.
The remote origin is https://github.com/arghya05/ap-forecast-sample.git; main and dev track origin, and feature/story has no upstream configured yet.
No Databricks, database or other workspace is used by ap_forecast.
CI is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py and enforces coverage >= 90 (COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0), no print/eval/exec, no bare except and lines at most 140 characters.
ci.py imports the third-party coverage package.
The current ap_forecast version is 0.9.0 and TSK-03 owns its version step.
predict_delay_days(history) and build_explanation_request(vendor, predicted_days, config=None) exist today; TSK-03 uses the first unchanged and TSK-04 adds risk=None to the second.
The repository memory requires keeping existing public signatures and names branches feature/<story>.

open_questions: RAQ-1: feat.tasks and the repository memory name branches feature/<story>, but the branch created is literally feature/story. Should TSK-03 (STORY-03) and TSK-04 (STORY-04) share it or get per-story branches? Interim: both tasks on feature/story, each commit prefixed with its story ID.

RAQ-2: ci.py needs the third-party coverage package. This step allowed no shell commands, so I couldn't check whether it is installed for /usr/bin/python3. Interim: assume it is; the first CI run will confirm.
RAQ-3: Push permission to origin wasn't tested because only the spine pushes. Write access is taken from tool:repo-access.
structured.summary: I fixed the G2 refusals: every repository file the output cites was read again in this attempt, and task.repo_access.md was rewritten in full. The result is unchanged. ap_forecast is the only repository the Data Science lane needs (TSK-03, TSK-04), so nothing has to be created. The branch feature/story is checked out at d67e866, the working tree is clean, the agent identity has write access, and no Databricks or database is used. The baseline is version 0.9.0, a CI bar of at least 90% coverage plus static checks, and the existing predict_delay_days and build_explanation_request functions the tasks extend. Three open questions remain, none of them blocking: the branch naming, whether the coverage package is installed, and that remote push permission couldn't be tested.
